transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-06
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Nexis CTO), Priya Rao (Nexis Lead ML Eng), Tom Baker (Nexis DevOps)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Quick migration demo to show parity mapping from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together to Redwood API. Covered endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings), streaming & function calling differences, rate limits and quotas, model mapping suggestions, security (SOC2/SSO/KMS) and next steps for POC and benchmarks.

-- Transcript --
[00:00] Jenna Park: All right hi everybody, thanks for joining, I'm Jenna from Redwood, and with me is Samir who's going to walk through the mapping and demo. Can you hear us all right?
[00:05] Alex Gomez: Yep, loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up. We're excited — trying to figure out migration path from OpenAI and Anthropic across a handful of services.
[00:12] Priya Rao: Hi, yeah we've got a mix of models in prod and a lot of prompt shaping, so parity is key.
[00:17] Samir Patel: Great. Real quick agenda — show API parity for chat/completions/embeddings, console walkthrough (routes, quotas), Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, then security and POC next steps. We'll demo a sample request that currently goes to OpenAI and map it to Redwood.
[00:29] Tom Baker: Also, Tom here — curious about private deployments, VPC peering and KMS.
[00:33] Jenna Park: We'll cover that. Quick note: transcription may mangle some names.

[02:10] Samir Patel: OK jumping in — here's a sample chat call you might be doing today with OpenAI: streaming via SSE with function-calling. On Redwood the equivalent is the chat endpoint, we support streaming and a compatible function-calling pattern. The key differences to watch are param names and streaming chunk formats.
[02:40] Priya Rao: Can you show the request/response side-by-side? We have a lot of tooling around function outputs so format stability is important.
[02:49] Samir Patel: Yep. So left is OpenAI style payload, right is Redwood. For example messages array is same concept, but note Redwood includes an optional 'role_hint' key in some SDKs — it's a small mismatch. Also we support named functions; we return call metadata in the streamed chunks slightly differently, sometimes the field is 'fn_call' in the stream vs 'function_call' in your current SDK.
[03:15] Alex Gomez: That's the kind of thing that trips our parser. Any SDKs or migration helpers?
[03:19] Jenna Park: We have SDK shims in the repo — a small compatibility layer that will map common OpenAI/Anthropic parameter names to Redwood equivalents. We'll share the script.

[04:05] Samir Patel: Embeddings — API is essentially the same: POST embeddings with model param, input list. One area to watch: tokenization differences and default normalization which can cause small distance shifts. For search / nearest-neighbor use cases we recommend reindexing embeddings and running a 1k sample evaluation.
[04:30] Priya Rao: Got it. We currently use a combined pipeline: embeddings from Together for semantic search and OpenAI for chat. Will Redwood handle mixed-model pipelines?
[04:39] Samir Patel: Yes, you can pin routes to different Redwood model variants — e.g., a high-accuracy model for embeddings and a faster cheaper model for chat. The console shows per-route model config and autoscaling.

[06:00] Tom Baker: On the infra side we need to understand rate-limits and burst behavior. We have spiky traffic.
[06:07] Jenna Park: For hosted we publish per-model QPS guidance and soft quotas, and Dedicated gives reserved capacity with predictable throughput. For spikes you can configure burst buckets; in Dedicated you can also set up autoscale policies. We'll include our recommended config for your traffic profile.

[08:20] Samir Patel: Demo time — I'm going to run a live chat request that currently hits OpenAI. First, here's the OpenAI cURL... (brief typing sounds) ...and now here's the Redwood equivalent. Streaming chunks — you can see tokens labeled 'delta' streaming through. Note slight differences: our chunk includes 'partial_text' and occasionally the model name abbreviation, which some parsers ignore.
[09:05] Priya Rao: The stream looks fine, but what about function calling vs tool integrations? We heavily use tool calls to query internal dbs.
[09:12] Samir Patel: We support remote tool invocation patterns; the recommended approach is the same: return a structured JSON payload from the model and call the tool in your app. Redwood's Console can also register 'trusted functions' so you get richer telemetry. There was a small difference in hyphenation of function names in the sample — transcriber might show 'tool-call' vs 'toolcall' — we'll get you the exact mapping.

[11:45] Alex Gomez: Security — can you recap SSO, audit logs, and key management? We need SOC2 and SAML at a minimum.
[11:51] Jenna Park: Sure. Hosted includes SOC2 reports and SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC at the org/route level, and audit logs. For encryption we support customer-managed keys via KMS integrations; for Private deployments you can also use HSM. We'll attach our security whitepaper and the SOC2 artifact.
[12:25] Priya Rao: For Private — what's the deployment model? VPC peering? On-prem?
[12:30] Samir Patel: We have two private flavors: Private Cloud (VPC peering or PrivateLink) where control plane still runs managed, and On-Prem which is an air-gapped package we install. Both support KMS integration and audit logging. The comp-sim — sorry, the transcriber often calls it 'comp sim' — but the idea is you keep control over data in both models.

[15:00] Tom Baker: How about model quantization and runtime differences? We currently use INT8 in some pipelines.
[15:07] Samir Patel: Redwood Optimize will suggest quantization profiles per-workload. Our runtime supports quantized execution paths and the kernel selection will choose the lowest precision that meets your latency/quality SLOs. In POC we usually run a small matrix: float16 baseline, int8 quantized, and check qual/regressions on a holdout prompt set.

[17:30] Priya Rao: That aligns with what we need. One concern — does Redwood expose per-token cost breakdowns? We need to reconcile bills against team estimates.
[17:38] Jenna Park: Yes, Console has token-level cost and latency breakdowns, per-route and per-model. For Dedicated we can provide cost modeling and you can attach budget alerts.

[20:10] Samir Patel: Back to parity mapping — here's a spreadsheet view. Column A is OpenAI/Anthropic/Together param, Column B is Redwood equivalent, Column C is migration notes. Example: "max_tokens" maps to same param; but "stop" handling differs slightly for multiline stop tokens — we recommend explicit stop token normalization.
[20:35] Priya Rao: Any gotchas with temperature and logprobs?
[20:40] Samir Patel: Logprobs support is present but for large seq lengths you might see performance trade-offs. Temperature behaves the same but the underlying sampling kernel may produce small differences; that's normal.

[23:00] Alex Gomez: For our POC we want to compare quality and cost for three flows: chat (multiturn), embeddings (semantic search), and batch generation (reports). Timeline target is end of quarter.
[23:10] Jenna Park: Sounds good. Typical POC plan: 1) parity mapping + infra checklist, 2) reindex a sample corpus for embeddings, 3) run head-to-head benchmarks for latency/throughput/cost, 4) review results and adjust model/quantization. We'll propose a two-week POC and a gate criteria doc.

[26:45] Tom Baker: On networking — how do we handle private keys and secrets?
[26:50] Samir Patel: For hosted we recommend KMS+env var rotation. For Dedicated you can bring your own key and in Private you can use HSM. We'll share the ops-runbook for credential rotation and least-privilege examples.

[30:00] Priya Rao: About prompts — we use prompt templating heavily and few system messages to guide the model. Any tooling to preserve prompt provenance?
[30:07] Jenna Park: Console keeps per-route prompt snapshots and we've got eval tooling in Optimize that can tie prompt sets to quality regression alerts. If you tag prompt versions we can correlate cost and latency over time.

[33:20] Samir Patel: Quick demo of Console — route config, model pinning, quota settings, rollout options. Here you can do canary deploys and automatic fallback to smaller models if SLOs drop. Also, the tracing hooks show token-level timing so you can see where tokens are being spent.
[35:05] Alex Gomez: That fallback policy is interesting. If we fall back, do we get a warning or is it silent?
[35:10] Samir Patel: You can set alerts and an explicit header in responses that indicates fallback happened. It's configurable.

[38:00] Priya Rao: A question — we use Together's models for embeddings because cost was good, will Redwood support model family with similar performance?
[38:08] Samir Patel: We have multiple verified embeddings models and can recommend one that matches your recall/latency tradeoffs. In some cases quantized variants give same accuracy at much lower cost. We'll include candidate models in the parity doc.

[41:50] Tom Baker: Let's talk SLA and uptime for Dedicated. We need 99.9% and a plan for incident response.
[41:56] Jenna Park: Dedicated comes with SLA options; we'll include the SLA doc and the oncall/incident flow. You also get dedicated capacity monitoring and on-call contacts.

[45:00] Alex Gomez: Ok, recap and next steps?
[45:05] Jenna Park: Recap: we'll send parity mapping spreadsheet, sample SDK shims, security artifacts (SOC2, whitepaper), and a proposed POC plan + checklist. Samir will send infra checklist and sample payloads. Priya will share prompts and token distribution. Tom will follow up on network constraints for Private.
[45:30] Priya Rao: Confirming timelines: we'd like the parity doc by tomorrow and the checklist in two days.
[45:36] Jenna Park: We'll hit those. Jenna: action items — I will email everything by EOD tomorrow (2025-11-07). Samir will provide the infra checklist by 11/08.

[47:10] Alex Gomez: Anything else on pricing? Can you give rough numbers for hosted vs Dedicated?
[47:15] Jenna Park: We'll include a pricing estimate in the follow-up email — hosted per-token estimates and Dedicated commit examples. For initial benchmarking we often recommend hosted to move fast unless data residency/SLA requires Dedicated.

[50:00] Tom Baker: One last operational quirk — our current parser depends on the exact field name for streaming events. Will the SDK shim keep the same names as OpenAI so we minimize changes?
[50:09] Samir Patel: The shim maps common patterns to minimize breakage; for anything custom we'll help you migrate the parser.

[51:30] Jenna Park: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the doc links and schedule the POC call.
[51:40] Alex Gomez: Thanks, appreciate it.
[51:43] Priya Rao: Thanks.
[51:45] Meeting ended.
